provider: NOAA Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services (CO-OPS)

request_contract.parameter_rules: Frozen one-day probe only: begin_date=20260101&end_date=20260101&station=9414290&product=water_level&datum=MLLW&time_zone=gmt&units=metric&application=OpenCatastrophe&format=json. San Francisco station 9414290, 2026-01-01 UTC, six-minute observations relative to Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW), metric metres. Exactly one GET to /api/prod/datagetter, no redirects and at most 1048576 bytes. The script constructs the entire HTTPS URL; no user-supplied URL, host, station, dates, product, datum, timezone, units, headers or extra parameters. One-day metadata/shape probe only; no raw data persistence, crawling or model admission.

response_contract.format: NOAA CO-OPS Data API JSON response for bounded water-level observations.
response_contract.scientific_semantics: CO-OPS water-level values are station observations whose interpretation depends on the requested station, product, datum, time zone, units and provider verification/quality state. Connectivity alone does not establish a hazard event, spatial footprint, return period, modelled loss or insured loss. Any later scientific use must preserve the exact request parameters, observation timestamps, datum and provider quality/verification semantics rather than treating the values as interchangeable generic sea level.

operational_constraints.rate_limit_notes: NOAA CO-OPS documents automated machine-to-machine API access but throttles high-volume clients. This probe issues one small historical-day request only, no retries, paging, scheduling, bulk crawl or other stations; any expansion requires distinct provider review.
operational_constraints.mutability_notes: Six-minute water-level observations may be revised and verification/quality status can change. Retain query identity, retrieval UTC, response byte length, SHA-256 and script hash as the receipt; this probe does not persist raw observations. Datum MLLW is a tidal reference, not local flood depth above ground or NAVD88.

rights_and_policy.notes: CO-OPS government data are public domain unless specifically annotated, with attribution requested and no misrepresentation of modified material as official NOAA data. NOAA's published Web Services page explicitly supports automated machine-to-machine retrieval; the Data API page requires an application identifier and documents throttling and short 6-minute limits. These findings support this one fixed small anonymous operational capability probe, not unlimited/commercial bulk use, redistribution of other sources, scientific admission or insurer-loss modelling.

expected_evidence: HTTP 200 anonymous fixed GET with expected JSON media type and station 9414290 metadata
One UTC-day sequence of at most 240 six-minute timestamped, finite water-level observations with provider flags
Small receipt containing retrieval UTC, exact fixed query, byte count, response SHA-256 and execution-script SHA-256; no provider measurements retained

notes: The fixed San Francisco 2026-01-01 CO-OPS request returned NOAA JSON water-level observations on 2026-11-02 (transient outside-repository connectivity check). A bounded repository probe with strict station/date/response validation is now specified, but a successful probe remains a connectivity/shape receipt only. No provider raw bytes, scientific validation, hazard catalogue, model input, insured exposure or insurance loss is admitted.
